brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact despite intraday selloff; HBM tightness extends to 2027, CoWoS gap narrowing
brief.summary: <cite index="39-4,39-16">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rallied 5.3% and 13% respectively on June 25</cite> after <cite index="39-8">Micron earnings fueled expectations that semiconductor supply shortages could persist through 2028</cite>, but <cite index="42-2,42-3">both names sold off ~3-4% on June 26 alongside broader Asia tech weakness</cite>. <cite index="11-2,11-7">DRAM contract prices jumped 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, following a record 90-95% increase in Q1, while NAND surged 70-75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="21-1,21-2">Hyperscaler capex for 2026 has topped $700 billion and continues rising</cite>, sustaining structural HBM demand that <cite index="9-3,9-10">drove SK Hynix to record Q1 revenue of ₩52.6tn ($35.5bn) and operating profit of ₩37.6tn ($27.8bn)</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="10-11">SK Hynix held 57% HBM market share in Q4 2025 vs Samsung's 22%</cite>, but <cite index="10-1,10-2">Samsung began shipping 12-layer HBM4E samples in late May, more than 20% faster than HBM4</cite>, signaling Samsung's catch-up momentum. <cite index="2-24">UBS forecasts SK Hynix will secure ~70% of HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>, cementing structural share advantage. However, <cite index="41-8,41-9">Samsung trades at 8.1x 2026E P/E vs SK Hynix at 9.2x, both significantly below global peers</cite>. Near-term tactical edge to SK Hynix on HBM share; medium-term re-rating opportunity favors Samsung on valuation compression and foundry optionality as <cite index="10-12,10-13">TSMC advanced-node capacity remains fully booked for years, raising Samsung foundry allocation expectations</cite>.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-11">BofA forecasts 2026 DRAM revenue +51% YoY and NAND +45% YoY, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively</cite>. <cite index="4-1">Goldman Sachs projects a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026</cite>. <cite index="16-11,16-12">This is a structural reallocation to HBM, not cyclical shortage; new fab capacity will not arrive in volume before late 2027, with meaningful relief pushed to 2028-2029</cite>. <cite index="7-9">AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026</cite>, and <cite index="16-13">HBM requires a 3-to-1 wafer capacity trade ratio with DDR5</cite>. Pricing momentum decelerating from parabolic Q1 but remains elevated; <cite index="15-11,15-12">buyers stopped chasing spot quotes in late May/early June, signaling parabolic phase maturing into plateau, not peak</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-15">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market at $54.6bn, +58% YoY</cite>, with <cite index="2-16">Goldman forecasting HBM demand for custom ASIC chips to skyrocket +82%, accounting for one-third of market</cite>. <cite index="2-18,2-19">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026; Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS are selecting HBM3E as optimal solution</cite>. Supply fully allocated: <cite index="37-16">HBM supply is fully allocated through 2026, including HBM3E, per SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Q3 earnings</cite>. <cite index="10-6">Samsung's customers include AMD, Nvidia, and Google</cite>; <cite index="10-9,10-10">Anthropic named Samsung a strategic infrastructure partner in latest funding round at $965bn valuation</cite>. <cite index="7-15">SK Hynix dedicated its massive Cheongju M15X mega-fab entirely to next-gen memory production</cite>. No relief until 2027+.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung ships HBM4E samples, 20% faster than HBM4
news_pulse.implication: Samsung narrows HBM technology gap vs SK Hynix; 12-layer HBM4E using 1c DRAM process and 4nm foundry base die signals aggressive roadmap execution. Shares rallied 6.5% on May 29 on the news.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix to announce massive investment packages June 29
news_pulse.implication: Samsung Group reportedly unveiling ₩1,000tn ($646bn) spending package over next decade per Maeil Business; executives attending presidential briefing. Market sold off -9% on June 26 in 'sell the fact' dynamic ahead of announcement.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex tops $700bn, rising to $1tn+ in 2027
news_pulse.implication: Meta raised 2026 capex to $125-145bn; Alphabet spent $35.67bn in Q1 alone (+100% YoY); Microsoft added $30.88bn in fiscal Q3 (+84% YoY). Structural demand floor for HBM/DRAM remains intact.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity reaching 120-140k wafers in 2026, plus 50-60k from OSAT partners; total ~200k/month. Nvidia secured >60% of 2025-2026 capacity. CoWoS bottleneck easing sequentially but still sold out through 2026.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q1 contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ, Q2 up 58-63% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Record Q1 rally decelerating but still extreme; NAND +70-75% QoQ in Q2. Memory shortage is structural reallocation to HBM, not cyclical. Enterprise SSD demand from AI deployments absorbing all incremental NAND capacity.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung Q1 semiconductor profit ₩53.7tn, SK Hynix revenue ₩52.6tn
news_pulse.implication: Samsung semiconductor OP ₩53.7tn ($36.1bn) = 94% of company total; SK Hynix OP ₩37.6tn ($27.8bn) on revenue of ₩52.6tn ($35.5bn), both Q1 2026 records. Warns memory shortages could last until 2027+.

news_pulse.headline: BofA names SK Hynix global memory 'Top Pick' for supercycle
news_pulse.implication: BofA defines 2026 as 'supercycle similar to 1990s boom'; forecasts HBM market could surpass entire 2024 DRAM market by 2028. SK Hynix positioned as primary beneficiary with HBM3E/HBM4 dual-generation supply capability.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI rallied 5.4% June 25, then sold off -3 to -4% June 26
news_pulse.implication: Samsung +5.3%, SK Hynix +13% on June 25 post-Micron beat; both reversed -3 to -4% on June 26 amid profit-taking and US PCE inflation concerns (4.1% YoY). SK Hynix ADR listing and JPM KOSPI 15k target provide medium-term support.

brief.derivatives_signal: June 26 intraday selloff triggered KOSPI 200 futures -5% sidecar circuit breaker; aggressive profit-taking after June 25 surge suggests short-term tactical positioning skewed long into earnings (Samsung early July, SK Hynix late July). Implied vol likely elevated. No structured positioning data available in payload.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung/SK Hynix official capex announcement June 29 (₩1,000tn Samsung package rumored); confirmation vs denial will drive next leg
US session response to Asia memory selloff; Micron ADR and WDC price action as proxy for whether profit-taking is regional or structural concern
KOSPI stabilization vs continuation below 8,200; June 25 low ~8,471 now broken, next support unclear
